cases.note: Five clause numbers, each with a different dash: U+2010, U+2011, U+2013, U+2014 and U+2212 all fold to a hyphen
U+2012 and U+2015 fold, and so does the fullwidth hyphen-minus through NFKC; U+2016 is just outside the range, so it separates
NFKC turns a ligature into letters and fullwidth digits into ASCII digits
NFKC turns superscript digits into digits, so each is part of its word
NFKC composes e plus a combining accent; a non-ASCII capital is lowercased; accents are kept
A soft hyphen is deleted, so the word stays whole
Empty input gives no tokens
Whitespace only, including a no-break space (NFKC makes it a space), gives no tokens
Punctuation, brackets and quotation marks separate words; case is folded
Both apostrophes, the ampersand and a hyphen in a compound separate words
An underscore separates words
Thousands separators are removed from a number; $ and % separate
A comma is a thousands separator only before exactly three digits that are not followed by a digit
A decimal followed by a letter does not take the number shape; the word shape takes 1 and then 5x
A three-digit fraction has the clause shape and gets no ancestors or alias; letters and digits together form one word
A dash between two numbers separates them; the dot after pp is punctuation
Each of the six identifier shapes stays whole
A citation as typed: the key stays whole, the rest separates
Paragraph groups stay part of the clause number
A paragraph group holds at most four characters; a longer group ends the clause number
An unbalanced parenthesis ends the clause number at the last complete group
A claim id or source id followed by a letter fails the boundary, so the parts become words
The clause shape fails the boundary and is not retried shorter; the number shape takes 252.204 and the suffix becomes a word
Near misses: xc-5 has the conflict shape, q-1234 has four digits and is not a question id
Near miss: four letters in the area, so not a claim id
Near miss: three digits, so not a source id
An identifier cannot start inside a word, so ts-0042 and xs-0042-v2 are plain words and numbers
Ancestors from the longest to the shortest, ending at the part and section; no alias because the suffix has one digit
A part and section alone has no ancestors
Ancestors, then the four-digit suffix as the alias
A suffix of two digits or of five digits gets no alias
A paragraph group with no hyphen suffix
A source version also emits its source id
Claim, question and conflict ids have no extras
A repeated clause number repeats its extras; the index side keeps duplicates
Duplicates are removed after case folding, keeping the first

cases.input: alpha alpha bravo charlie delta echo foxtrot golf hotel india juliet kilo lima mike
cases.note: Duplicates are removed first, then the first 12 tokens are kept; mike is dropped
The query side emits no ancestors and no alias
Surrounding whitespace is ignored
A bare four-digit number is an ordinary number token on the query side
